analysis.title: GS Crook - 2 Mins Read: How could Major CB's surprise this week...? 27 Oct 2026
key_insights: Fed: Warsh is likely to echo Waller's 'hikes don't need to come at consecutive meetings' and say there is no pre-set pace. This likely keeps hike premium priced into 2027.

Fed: The clearest misstep risk is a repeat of July, when Warsh's most dovish answers came while explaining why the Fed wasn't hiking. If he focuses on the current decision rather than the path, the market could read the presser as dovish.
Fed: More airtime on inflation likely extends curve flattening and keeps the front end selling off. More discussion of tighter financial conditions likely re-steepens the curve.
Fed: With about 75bps priced through Q3 2027, a 15bp rally is more likely than a selloff. In FX, AUDUSD likely moves most on a surprise hawkish Fed.
Fed: The market prices 3bps for the October meeting and 20 more for December (23bps cumulative through December). Both the desk and the market expect a skip on Wednesday.

ECB: The statement is not expected to mention sovereign spreads. Lagarde will likely call France a political problem rather than a monetary one, and add that the ECB has tools to contain contagion and keep policy transmission working.
ECB: The bigger risk for EUR fixed income and Bunds is a dismissive or very hawkish tone on French spreads, which would leave markets feeling an ECB backstop is far away.
ECB: Fewer hikes would be bearish for EUR and bullish for Bunds. A focus on credit easing or transmission tools would be bullish for EUR and the periphery.

ECB: Winter TTF is 25% higher than at the September ECB meeting and 40% higher than at end-September. The Oat/Bund spread widened from 90bps at the September meeting to almost 180bps at one stage last week. The desk sees the key risk as a somewhat more hawkish ECB than the market expects.
BoJ: The base case is a mildly dovish pause at 1.25%, with underlying inflation converging toward 2%. The Board will likely cut its FY26 core inflation forecast and raise FY27 on energy.

BoJ: The BoJ will not push back against a December hike (~80% priced), mindful of the risk of USDJPY rising back above 160. With the market already priced for it and Western core CPI running at 4% annualized over the last 3 months, the market could set a higher bar for what counts as a hawkish meeting.
BoJ: Short covering in rates has largely concluded after the recent JGB rally. The desk expects a gradual post-meeting sell-off and keeps its medium-term view of a 2.00%+ terminal rate.
US rates strategy expects the BoJ to leave the market pricing sustained rather than strongly front-loaded hike risk. It sees the 5y part of the curve skewed toward underperformance.

risk_factors: Warsh's presser reads dovish because he focuses on the current decision rather than the path, as happened in July.
Lagarde is dismissive or very hawkish on French spreads, leaving markets feeling an ECB backstop is far away.
The ECB is more hawkish than the market expects, given the 40% October rally in winter TTF.
The BoJ is read as hawkish despite the December hike already being ~80% priced, with USDJPY risk back above 160.
A hot September core PCE print on Friday.
vol_and_positioning: G10 options: cheapest USD calls remain USDJPY, with surprisingly high premium still for USD puts there (1m risk reversal 2.15, not far off the year's highs).
AUDUSD would likely be the largest mover in the case of a surprise Fed hike. Implied gaps in most of G10 are 45-55bps.
Team PE's favourite ECB trade is to buy 6m options funded by either 1m window knock-outs or 1m strangles, with the curve inverted 1m-3m.
USDJPY has been range trading for a while. Trade-weighted JPY is close to the year's highs, which reduces intervention risk, and global growth concerns prevent a fast move back higher.
Fed rate hike odds were briefly 50/50 after the hot CPI and have since fallen back to a low probability, which G10 options trading calls surprising.
geopolitical: Energy prices are near the post-US/Iran conflict highs.
Stress in French sovereign spreads, which Lagarde is expected to frame as a political rather than a monetary problem.

tension_points.bull_case: A clear message of no pre-set pace and hikes at any time keeps hike premium priced into 2027, with roughly 75bps priced through Q3 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Warsh focuses on the current decision and the October skip, and the market reads it as dovish, as in July. A 15bp rally is more likely than a selloff.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A presser that gives more airtime to tighter financial conditions than to inflation risks would re-steepen the curve and read dovish.

tension_points.bull_case: Lagarde frames France as a political problem and notes the ECB has tools to contain contagion and keep transmission working.
tension_points.bear_case: A dismissive or very hawkish tone on French spreads leaves markets feeling an ECB backstop is far away.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A move toward credit easing or transmission tools would be bullish for EUR and the periphery.
